subcategory_description: Means-tested help for people over State Pension age on a low income.
subject_intro: How much Pension Credit tops up a pensioner's weekly income to, the extra amounts for disability and caring, and Savings Credit.
subject_meta_title: Pension Credit 2026/27: £238 a Week Single, £363.25 for Couples
subject_meta_description: Pension Credit for 2026/27 tops weekly income up to £238 for a single person and £363.25 for a couple, plus extra amounts and Savings Credit.
label: Guarantee Credit for a single person (weekly)
context: Pension Credit tops up a single person's weekly income to this amount.

label: Guarantee Credit for a couple (weekly)
context: Pension Credit tops up a couple's joint weekly income to this amount.

label: Extra for a severe disability (weekly)
context: Added if you get a qualifying disability benefit, such as Attendance Allowance or the daily living part of PIP.

label: Extra if you care for another adult (weekly)
context: Added if you get, or have claimed, Carer's Allowance or Carer Support Payment.

label: Most Savings Credit for a single person (weekly)
context: Only for people who reached State Pension age before 6 April 2016 and saved for retirement, for example in a personal pension.

label: Most Savings Credit for a couple (weekly)
context: The most a couple can get in Savings Credit, under the same rules as for a single person.

subcategory_description: Tax relief on pension contributions, tax-free lump sums and the age you can take a private pension.
subject_intro: How much tax relief you get on what you pay into a pension, the limits on it, and the extra relief higher-rate taxpayers can claim.
subject_meta_title: Pension Tax Relief 2026/27: Rates and Limits
subject_meta_description: Pension tax relief explained: 20% added automatically, extra relief for higher-rate taxpayers, and the limits of 100% of earnings or £2,880 without earnings.
label: Basic rate tax relief
context: With relief at source, your pension provider claims this from the government and adds it to your pot.

label: Most you can pay in with tax relief (share of earnings)
context: Tax relief on your own contributions is limited to 100% of your earnings in the tax year. HMRC can reclaim relief above this.

label: Most you can pay in with relief if you have no earnings
context: Your provider can claim 20% relief on contributions up to this each tax year, if you have no earnings.

label: Extra relief you can claim at the higher rate
context: Claimed through Self Assessment on contributions up to the amount of income you paid 40% tax on (England, Wales and NI).

label: Extra relief you can claim at the additional rate
context: Claimed on contributions up to the amount of income you paid 45% tax on (England, Wales and NI).
Contributions above this in a tax year, including your employer's, can face a tax charge.

subject_intro: How much of your pension you can take tax-free, and the two lifetime limits on tax-free lump sums that replaced the lifetime allowance.
subject_meta_title: Tax-Free Pension Lump Sum: 25% and the £268,275 Allowance
subject_meta_description: You can usually take 25% of a pension tax-free, up to the £268,275 lump sum allowance, with a £1,073,100 limit including death benefits.
label: Share of a pension you can take tax-free
context: You can usually take up to this share of any pension as a tax-free lump sum, up to the lump sum allowance.

subject_intro: The earliest age you can take money from a workplace or personal pension without a tax charge, and the rise due in April 2028.
subject_meta_title: Minimum Pension Age: 55 Now, Rising to 57 in April 2028
subject_meta_description: You can usually take a private pension from age 55. The normal minimum pension age rises to 57 from 6 April 2028.
label: Minimum pension age now
context: The earliest age most people can take money from a workplace or personal pension, unless they retire due to ill health.

label: Minimum pension age from 6 April 2028
context: Applies unless you have a protected pension age. Taking benefits earlier without one leads to a tax charge.
The State Pension is separate. You can usually take a private pension well before State Pension age.

label: Increase for each year you defer
context: Your State Pension rises by 1% for every 9 weeks you put off claiming, if you reached State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016.

label: Shortest deferral that earns an increase
context: You must put off claiming for at least this long before your State Pension goes up.

label: Employee minimum contribution
context: What you pay if you've been automatically enrolled. Your employer can pay more so you pay less, as long as the 8% total is met.

label: Monthly earnings for an employer contribution if you opt in
context: If you join a workplace pension voluntarily, your employer only has to pay in if you earn more than this a month.
